content.title: About
content.content: Light Ranch dressing is a reduced‑fat version of the classic Ranch sauce, made with low‑fat yogurt, kefir or skim milk. It retains the creamy, garlicky, herbaceous flavor of traditional Ranch while delivering fewer calories and less fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ranch is the best‑selling salad dressing in the United States and is commonly used as a dip for vegetables and chicken wings.
The light version was introduced in the early 2000s to meet growing demand for lower‑calorie condiments.
Typical ingredients include yogurt, kefir, dill, garlic, onion powder, and spices, making it more protein‑rich than the original mayonnaise‑based recipe.
Unlike the classic sauce, the light variant often contains no added sugar.
Chefs frequently use Ranch as a base for creating new flavor blends.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Light Ranch provides roughly 50‑70 kcal per 30 g serving, making it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Higher protein
items.content: The yogurt/kefir base supplies about 2‑3 g of protein per serving, helping to promote satiety.

items.title: Calcium and probiotics
items.content: Dairy components deliver calcium and live cultures that support bone health and gut microbiota.

items.title: Reduced saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional Ranch, the light version contains minimal saturated fat, which is better for cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dairy base provides vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains dairy, so it may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Those allergic to casein or whey should avoid this dressing.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some commercial versions are high in salt; individuals monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Preservatives and flavorings
items.content: Processed varieties may include additives that are not suitable for clean‑eating diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Light Ranch works well as a salad dressing, dip for carrots, celery, crackers, and as a sauce for baked chicken, fish, or fries. It can be drizzled on sandwiches, wraps, and burgers to add creaminess without excess calories.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container. After opening, it typically lasts 7‑10 days. Discard if you notice off‑smells, discoloration, or mold.
